_readme: English-only copy: the study pages (/principles/ and /principles/N/: intro, legacies, thirtySix, logoStory), the English half of the 404 page (notFound; its Spanish twin is in the front matter of src/pages/404.njk) and the one-paragraph event summary used by the JSON-LD and the calendar file (jsonld.eventSummary). The workshop pages have their own bilingual files in src/_data/pagecopy/. Write the email, date, times and Zoom numbers only as tokens ({email}, {date}, {time}…). Fields read through | md accept simple Markdown.

intro._readme: /principles/: the heading and the two short paragraphs below the twelve number tiles, the first section after the hero (body accepts simple Markdown).
intro.heading: Pull one thread and the whole cloth moves
body: Most of us met the Steps first, from someone who had been where we were. The Traditions came later, usually when a group business meeting got lively. The Concepts, if we met them at all, arrived with a service job we did not quite ask for. We tend to keep the three in separate drawers.

Look at number **one**. Step One admits powerlessness, Tradition One puts our common welfare first, and Concept I places final authority in the conscience of the whole Fellowship. Written years apart, the three say the same thing: none of us gets well alone.

legacies._readme: /principles/: the three legacy cards. Each card's name, blurb and literature come from site.json → legacies, and its aa.org link from principles.json → sources.
legacies.heading: Three legacies, one Fellowship
legacies.lead: At the St. Louis convention in 1955, Bill W. handed A.A. to its members in the form of three legacies: Recovery, Unity and Service. They were never meant to be studied apart.

thirtySix._readme: /principles/ (page title, hero lead, meta description, the side-by-side table and the one link back to the workshop) and, under numberPage, the headings and labels of /principles/1/ … /principles/12/. The 36 principles themselves are in principles.json.
thirtySix.title: The 36 Principles
thirtySix.lead: Take any number from one to twelve. The Step, the Tradition and the Concept that carry it are three expressions of one idea, seen from the chair, from the group and from the Fellowship as a whole.
thirtySix.description: All 36 principles of A.A. side by side: the Twelve Steps, Twelve Traditions and Twelve Concepts for World Service, with the thread that runs through each number.
thirtySix.tableLead: All 36 in one table, each with its principle word and a one-line summary. To read one legacy straight through, show it on its own.
thirtySix.tableCaption: The 36 principles: for each number, the Step, the Tradition and the Concept, each with a principle word and a one-line summary.
thirtySix.companion: These study pages are a companion to The Incredible Tapestry, a free 1-day online A.A. workshop on {date}.

numberPage.questionsHeading: Questions for a meeting or a sponsor conversation
numberPage.questionsNote: In a group, read the Step, the Tradition and the Concept aloud, then share on the thread that connects them.

logoStory._readme: /principles/: the closing section beside the logo (body accepts simple Markdown).
logoStory.heading: About the mark
body: The circle and triangle have stood for A.A. since the 1950s: the circle is the whole world of A.A., and the three sides of the triangle are our Three Legacies, named here the way they appear on a medallion: Unity, Service, Recovery.

Inside, three circles overlap, one for each legacy in its own color: blue for Recovery, green for Unity and gold for Service. The small shape where all three meet is the tapestry itself: the Fellowship, held together by all 36 threads.

notFound.heading: That thread leads nowhere
notFound.body: The page you were looking for has moved or never existed. The whole tapestry is still here, though, starting from the front page.

jsonld.eventSummary: A free, 1-day online A.A. workshop on Zoom: a series of presentations on how the Steps, Traditions and Concepts weave this incredible tapestry, with plenty of time for sharing and asking questions. Spanish and ASL interpretation will be provided, and no pre-registration is required. It is similar to the Tapestry meetings held previously in Raynham, Massachusetts.
